title: fix(plugin-auth): the self-registration grant settles on the registrant's first membership (ADR-0131 D3, C8 8b-0f)
body:
Part of #24343
Part of #15212
Clause-②: no

C8 stage 8b-0f. It carries ruling Q1 A on #24377 (record 6257510973, item 1): the self-registration grant settles on the first membership. The card stays open because Q2 (stage 8b-0d) still lands on it.

## What changed

The declared self-registration set (`auth.audience.selfRegistrationPermissionSet`) is an assignment, and ADR-0131 D3 makes an assignment an organization row. So the grant is now written with the registrant's first membership and owned by that membership's organization, under every posture. Nothing is written to `sys_user_permission_set` without an organization.

All runtime changes are in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`:

- **`settleSelfRegistrationGrant`** (`user.create.after`). It consumes the admission stage as before, then reads the registrant's membership.
  - The registrant holds one (under `single`, the reconciler bound the Default Organization a moment earlier in the same hook; or a host hook provisioned an organization first). The grant lands now, owned by that organization.
  - The registrant holds none (a wall). No grant is written. A pending claim is persisted instead.
- **The pending claim** is a `sys_verification` row. Its `identifier` is `self-registration-grant:` plus the user id, its `value` is the set name, and it waits 365 days.
  - `sys_verification` is the auth layer's existing store of one-shot claims keyed on an identifier with an expiry. It survives a restart, and it has no organization column (ADR-0131 D1 fate 1, inventory `noColumn`).
  - No new object, no new column, no new field.
- **The first-membership seam.** `observeFirstMemberships` is registered once per engine, from the constructor. It is a middleware on `sys_member` inserts, the same seam plugin-security's `organization_admin` auto-grant uses. Every membership writer inserts through the engine: better-auth's organization create (the creator as owner), invitation acceptance and server-side add-member, the membership reconciler, the Default Organization bootstrap, and host hooks. One seam therefore covers all of them, with no hook per path.
- **`settleDeferredSelfRegistrationGrant`** consumes the claim first (read, delete by id), then writes the grant owned by that membership's organization. A later membership finds no claim and writes no second grant. The existing by-name check also holds.
- An engine with no middleware seam could never settle a claim. There, a registrant with no organization is reported ungranted at `error` at sign-up, and no claim is parked.
- **Helper pair, a minimal edit (named as the dispatch asks).** The doc comment on `derivableWriteOrganizationId` no longer lists the self-registration grant among its readers, because the grant does not read it any more. Its code and `authMailOrganizationArg` are unchanged, and no identity-mail send site was touched.

## Measured (A1–A5)

- **A1, the membership paths.** The writers of a user's `sys_member` row on this tree are: better-auth `organization/create` (owner) and `accept-invitation`, better-auth add-member, `reconcileMembership` (`user.create.after`, `session.create.before`, the one-time backfill), `ensureDefaultOrganization`'s owner bind, and host `user.create.after` hooks. All of them write through the data engine, so the `sys_member` insert middleware sees each one (#4802's corrected mechanism, quoted in `auth-manager.ts`). The walled dogfood pin drives the real better-auth organization create through it. Under `single`, the census pin shows the sign-up still ends with exactly one grant, owned by the Default Organization.
- **A2, persistence.** Admission decides "self-registrant" from the request: the creation class, the bootstrap probe and the pending-invitation lookup. None of those is stored. `sys_user.source` separates only `idp_provisioned` from `env_native`, and `sys_account.provider_id` is `credential` for admin-created users too. So no existing user or account field marks a self-registrant, and a persisted claim is needed. `sys_verification` is the narrowest existing store that fits: deployment-level, durable, and with an expiry better-auth already sweeps (`findVerificationValue` deletes expired rows). The `value` column is `internal`, so it is read back through `recoverInternalFieldsForSystemRead`.
- **A3, existing NULL grants.** Untouched here (the ceremony is 8b-0c's). Measurement and recommendation are in the report on #24343.
- **A4, pins.** See Tests.
- **A5, Clause-②.** `no`. No spec, schema, export or route changes. `AudienceConfigSchema.selfRegistrationPermissionSet` describes "the permission set granted to each self-registrant", and the settings manifest and its translations say the same. None of them promises the grant at sign-up time, and the generated reference page carries only that `describe`. No `packages/spec` byte moved.

## Tests (head `29b223ed3`)

- **New:** `plugin-auth/src/self-registration-grant-first-membership.test.ts`, 9 cases.
  - Under `single`: one grant, owned by the Default Organization, no claim.
  - Walled sign-up: 0 grants, 1 claim with no organization column.
  - The first membership: exactly 1 grant, owned by that organization, and the claim is consumed.
  - A second membership: no second grant.
  - A restart: a fresh manager over the same store settles the claim.
  - No claim (an invited user): no grant. An expired claim: no grant.
  - No middleware seam: reported at `error`, nothing parked.
  - Two managers on one engine: the seam is registered once.
- **New:** `dogfood/test/self-registration-grant-first-membership-walled.dogfood.test.ts`, 3 cases, real stack, `isolated` (`posture-only`), open audience. The sign-up writes no grant. `POST /auth/organization/create` lands exactly one, owned by the new organization. A second organization lands none.
- **Changed:**
  - `audience-posture.test.ts`: the four end-to-end "grant lands" cases now run `single` (a tenancy service), so the reconciler binds a membership, and one of them asserts the owner.
  - `find-envelope-limb-removal.test.ts`: the D4 grant-by-name case binds the membership first.
  - `producers-name-organization.test.ts`: its two grant cases are removed. The `single` one is re-pinned in the new file. The walled one asserted the behaviour this stage retires (a grant with no organization), and the new walled pins assert the opposite.
- **Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, EXIT trap). The claim write was mutated back to a sign-up grant with no organization (marker `ups_ABLATED_`, anchor 1→0, blob `debc7651`→`624afb11`). After the rebuild, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs`. The DTS step failed on TS6133 (the now-unused claim method), but the JS that the suite consumes was emitted.
  - The walled dogfood pin went red, 2 failed / 1 passed: the sign-up wrote a grant, and the organization grant read `null`.
  - The unit file went red, 5 failed / 4 passed.
  - Restore: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuild, preflight `--absent` exit 0, dogfood 3/3 green.
- **Suites, at `29b223ed3`:** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` test, 165 files, 3165 passed, 10 skipped; typecheck exit 0. Dogfood, after a plugin-auth rebuild: the walled pin, `signup-organization-census` (single) and `org-create-default-team` (walled), 3 files / 7 passed.
- **Gates, at `29b223ed3`:** `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths), 108 families plus the 51-row artifact roster, each exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reads: 108 derived, 108 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
  - Fixed on the way: `check-tenant-audit-census` (the riders below), `check:engine-double-contract` (ledger row), and `check:where-matcher` (the new double now refuses WHERE combinators).
  - Roster rows that need a PR context exited 2 (NOT WIRED) locally: `check-closing-target-claim`, `check-single-claim-paths`, and `check-governed-queue-guard` (no event payload, exit 1). CI's reading counts for those. `check-partof-closing-keyword`, run with this body as `PR_BODY`, exits 0.

## Riders

- **`content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`.** These were regenerated (`node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`) and the page's prose figures updated, because `check-tenant-audit-census` holds them to the census and this stage moves the write-call-site population from 229 to 231. The three plugin-auth writes state `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` at the call, so they count as elevated. The "cite `2 / N`" provable-yield figure stays 2.
- **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`:** one row for the new test's `delete` double (`check-engine-double-contract --write`).

## Acceptance notes

- The claim waits 365 days. A registrant who first joins an organization later holds only the deployment's baseline. Cloud's report (cloud#3051) shows its self-registration set is also its `isDefault` baseline, so nothing changes there.
- Under `single` with `membershipPolicy: 'invite-only'`, a self-registrant gets no membership at sign-up, so the grant now waits for the first membership there too, as the ruling's "under every posture" says. Under `auto` (the default), `single` is unchanged.
